approachQuestion.prompt:
Assembly Formula. A non-empty binary tree describes an arithmetic formula. A leaf stores an integer. Every internal node stores one operator from +, -, * and has exactly two children. Return the formula value, taking the left child as the first operand and the right child as the second.

Example 1: Input: -( *(3,4), +(2,5) ). Output: 5, because 12-7=5. Example 2: Input: -(2,9). Output: -7. Example 3: Input: leaf -6. Output: -6. Parentheses in this notation indicate children, not an extra operator.

Constraints: 1 <= n <= 199999 nodes; leaf values are between -1000 and 1000. Every intermediate and final result fits a signed 64-bit integer. The immutable tree has child pointers only, no cycles or shared nodes; shape is unrestricted. Operator nodes are explicitly distinguished from integer leaves. Do not rewrite or reorder operands.

options.text: Use postorder frames holding a phase and fixed-size child results. After both children finish, apply the operator to left result then right result, and return the value to the parent.
options.feedback: A parent receives the complete values of its operands, and retaining which side produced each value preserves subtraction order.

options.text: At each node construct a fully parenthesized expression string by copying its complete child strings; parse and evaluate the root string exactly with 64-bit arithmetic.
options.feedback: Full parentheses preserve the formula, so this works. Repeatedly copying subtree text and parsing it is removable: the parent only needs the two child values.

options.text: Apply each internal operator as soon as the node is entered, using zero for any child value not yet computed, and never revise that result.
options.feedback: For +(2,3) the children are not computed on entry, so this returns 0 instead of 5.

options.text: Evaluate both child subtrees, then apply the parent operator with the larger child value first.
options.feedback: Subtraction is ordered. For -(2,9), this returns 7 instead of -7.

feedback.reason: Evaluate child results before their parent and preserve operand order for noncommutative operators.
details: Use explicit frames with entry, left-done, and right-done phases. A leaf returns its stored integer. An internal node saves the left result, obtains the right result, applies its operator in left-right order, and passes the resulting integer to its parent. Discard completed child frames.

Compute both child results before applying the parent's operator, preserving left/right operand order. Completed child frames can be released after returning their scalars; storing every subtree value is unnecessary.

“Use postorder frames holding a phase and fixed-size child results. After both children finish, apply the operator to left result then right result, and return the value to the parent.”: A parent receives the complete values of its operands, and retaining which side produced each value preserves subtraction order.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the revealed formula frame method let n be the node count and h the tree height in nodes. Choose the tight worst-case pair for time and auxiliary space. Include frames and saved operand values; exclude the tree and scalar result. All arithmetic fits the stated machine integer range and takes constant time; no strings are built.
constraints: All legal shapes are allowed; do not assume balance. Heights count nodes, not edges.

Pointer access, comparisons, arithmetic on the stated integer ranges, and allocation/release of a fixed-size frame take constant time. No hashing is used. Count all live explicit frames; the method does not use language recursion or copy paths/subtrees unless explicitly stated.

feedback.reason: Evaluate each node once using fixed-size frames on the active ancestor path.
details: Each node returns one value after constant work, including one operator application for an internal node. The active ancestor frames have fixed-size fields and use O(h) space; a full binary comb can attain this scale.
Induction on subtrees gives the exact value at every returned frame. Leaves give their integers; internal frames apply their specified operator to the correct ordered operand values.

“O(n) time, O(h) auxiliary space”: Each node returns one value after constant work, including one operator application for an internal node. The active ancestor frames have fixed-size fields and use O(h) space; a full binary comb can attain this scale.
“O(n²) time, O(h) auxiliary space”: Completed subtrees are not scanned again; nesting the control flow does not itself multiply the node visits.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The live explicit stack is auxiliary memory and can grow with tree height.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: This is a looser upper bound since h <= n; the height-sensitive bound is tighter and no full node table is retained.
